owned_invariants: With no rule to load, the seed comes back byte for byte and its two hashes are equal.

The rules written are exactly the ledger's admitted rules in id order, followed by the one rule under trial when the request names it. A proposed rule is never loaded unless it is named as under trial.
The rules follow the seed after one blank line, under a line that carries the first 16 hex digits of the ledger head, one line per rule: its id in brackets, then its constraint.
A rule whose id or constraint contains a line feed or a carriage return is refused as RULE_NOT_ONE_LINE, so a rule cannot write a second rule's line.
The account returned with the seed states the full ledger head, the entry count, the rules, the rule under trial and the SHA-256 of the base seed and of the loaded seed.
loaded recomputes the seed from the base seed and the ledger as it stood at the stated head and accepts only an exact match. It keeps answering the same for an old head after the ledger grows.
The ledger is replayed before anything is read from it; an edited ledger is refused as CHAIN_BROKEN.
boundaries: A loaded rule is text after the seed. Nothing here shows that a model obeys it.
The seed names 16 hex digits of the head; the full head is in the account, and loaded compares against the full head.
loaded shows that a seed is what the ledger loads. It does not show that a run used that seed; the workflow's replay binds a run to its task.

score.level_basis: Typed refusals on every failure path, closed requests, vocabularies from the canon, exact integers, no unwrap or direct indexing.
